title: Local Forge runs cross-origin POSTs: any web page can write the local inbox
body:
## Summary
tools/local-forge.mjs gates only the CORS read headers on Origin; a simple (text/plain) POST from any site, or a DNS-rebound host, still runs the resolver and writes the db.

## Description
tools/local-forge.mjs:223-225 sets access-control headers only for a local Origin, and tools/local-forge.mjs:232 refuses only an OPTIONS preflight from a foreign Origin. tools/local-forge.mjs:233-237 then runs POST /invoke for any Origin and any Content-Type: readBody (tools/local-forge.mjs:196-211) JSON-parses the body whatever its type, so a text/plain POST needs no preflight. No Host check exists either, so a DNS-rebinding page reads responses too. Every resolver is reachable, including writes (verdict.accept, settings.set, sample.load, direction.set in forge/src/core/app.mjs:235-271), and localPerms grants every permission (tools/local-forge/ports.mjs:260-264). The UI bridge already sends application/json (forge/static/app/src/dev/http-bridge.js:18), so requiring it costs the real client nothing.

## Flow
- A developer runs `npm run local:forge` (port 4710, package.json scripts.local:forge) and browses the web
- Any page fires fetch("http://127.0.0.1:4710/invoke", {method:"POST", mode:"no-cors", body: JSON.stringify({key:"verdict.reject", ...})})
- The resolver runs as local-user and the local inbox, rules and direction change; with DNS rebinding the page also reads cards and evidence quotes

## Expected impact
Closes a drive-by write (and with rebinding, read) path into the developer's local inbox, which holds real scan evidence of private repos. Fix: refuse POST unless content-type is application/json, refuse a present non-local Origin with 403, and refuse a Host that is not 127.0.0.1/localhost:<port>.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a foreign origin can no longer drive resolvers
Before: probe: POST /invoke with Origin https://evil.example and Content-Type text/plain answered 200 {"project_key":"dowser-sample","created":6}; /dev/state went from proposals 0 to 6, evidence 0 to 39; a request with Host attacker.example answered 200
After: the same two requests answer 403/415 and /dev/state is unchanged; the UI bridge (application/json, local origin) still works
Method: probe - ran the real server on a temp db outside the repo with curl; the after state needs the code change, so only before is measured
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/local-forge.mjs:232 `if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') { res.writeHead(origin && !cors['access-control-allow-origin'] ? 403 : 204, cors); res.end(); return; }`; tools/local-forge.mjs:233 `if (req.method === 'POST' && url.pathname === '/invoke') {` (no Origin/Host/content-type check); probe: `curl -X POST /invoke -H "Origin: https://evil.example" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data '{"key":"sample.load","payload":{}}'` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... {"project_key":"dowser-sample","created":6}`; /dev/state proposals 0 -> 6; `-H "Host: attacker.example:47199" /dev/state` -> 200
impact_why: Drive-by writes into the local inbox of anyone running local:forge; private-repo evidence readable via rebinding.

title: Run the gates in CI: no workflow exists, Dependabot PRs merge unchecked
body:
## Summary
The repo has .github/dependabot.yml and no .github/workflows at all, so typecheck, tests and the forge gates run only when an agent or person remembers.

## Description
git ls-files .github lists only .github/dependabot.yml. dependabot.yml:1-26 opens up to 5 weekly PRs in each of three ecosystems (/, /forge, /forge/static/app); none gets a status check. AGENTS.md:31-38 names the gates (`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, forge:typecheck/test/check-shared/build-ui) as a hand-run step. The suite has only ever run on Windows here (tests branch on process.platform at skill/scripts/tests/deps.test.mjs:208,211; tools/lens-eval.mjs:178-198), so a POSIX-only break is invisible. SECURITY.md:52-64 makes `npm run sbom` a hand step of each release too.

## Flow
- Dependabot opens a minor/patch group PR for forge/static/app
- Nothing runs; a reviewer merges on the diff
- The next session discovers a broken build-ui or typecheck after the fact

## Expected impact
One workflow (ubuntu + windows, Node 22.13 and current) running `npm ci`, typecheck, test and the forge gates turns every Dependabot PR and push into a checked change and catches platform drift.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every PR carries a gate result
Before: 0 workflow files; 0 status checks on Dependabot PRs; gates run on one Windows box
After: every push/PR runs the documented gates on two OSes
Method: simulation - adding CI is a repo change; walked three cases: a dependabot bump that breaks forge typecheck (caught on PR), a POSIX path bug (caught by ubuntu leg), a clean bump (green check)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: `git ls-files .github` -> `.github/dependabot.yml` only; `ls .github/workflows` -> No such file or directory; .github/dependabot.yml:3 `- package-ecosystem: npm` x3 with `open-pull-requests-limit: 5`; AGENTS.md:33 `Run both before you hand back work:`
impact_why: Up to 15 weekly dependency PRs and every push land with no automated gate; platform breaks surface late.

title: Test sample-capture: it writes the public sample inbox and has no test
body:
## Summary
tools/sample-capture.mjs exports parseArgs and capture (shaped for tests) and builds forge/src/sample/self-scan.json, yet no test imports it.

## Description
git grep finds no test naming tools/sample-capture.mjs (skill/scripts/tests and forge/test). The tool selects cards by status and run (tools/sample-capture.mjs:91), strips STORE_OWNED (:97), sorts deterministically (:61-66) and validates each record with Forge's checkRecord/areaProblem (:107-115). Its header promises "Output is deterministic for a given store" (:25-26) and that the file loads; neither is checked, and it mutates process.env.DOWSER_HOME as a side effect (:74). Five of the nine dev-tooling files have no test at all: dogfood, dogfood-decide, forge-live-e2e, quality-snapshot, sample-capture.

## Flow
- A store-schema change renames a column proposalRecord reads
- sample-capture still writes a file, now missing a field or refused by Forge on load
- The judge-facing sample inbox breaks on the next capture

## Expected impact
One test using _fixture.mjs: build a store with two verified cards in a done run, call capture(), assert schema dowser-sample/1, the fixed sort, no STORE_OWNED key, and byte-equal output on a second call; plus parseArgs refusing a credentialed --repo-url.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the sample file's promises are tested
Before: 0 tests for sample-capture
After: 1 test covering determinism and Forge acceptance
Method: simulation - walked a renamed column, a reserve card and a credentialed URL through capture/parseArgs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: `git grep -l "tools/sample-capture.mjs\|sample-capture.mjs'" -- '*.test.mjs' 'forge/test/*'` -> (none); tools/sample-capture.mjs:73 `export async function capture(o) {`; tools/sample-capture.mjs:25 `Output is deterministic for a given store`
impact_why: The sample inbox is what a judge without the skill sees first; its generator is unguarded.

title: Derive local-forge tools/list from the manifest; its header still says seven tools
body:
## Summary
tools/local-forge.mjs hand-copies twelve tool schemas from forge/manifest.yml; nothing checks the copy, and its usage header says "the seven forge-mcp-2 tools".

## Description
tools/local-forge.mjs:53 says the schemas come "from forge/manifest.yml"; tools/local-forge.mjs:56-91 retypes them (12 entries). The only check is skill/scripts/tests/local-forge-e2e.test.mjs:143-145, which compares names to a third hand-typed list and types to string|integer - not properties, required or descriptions against forge/manifest.yml:39-141. The names are also hand-kept in forge/src/core/app.mjs:52-54 (TOOL_NAMES). Today they agree (eyeballed property by property), but the next manifest change updates one copy. tools/local-forge.mjs:18-19 already drifted: "the seven forge-mcp-2 tools" while docs/contracts/forge-mcp-2.md:4 says twelve.

## Flow
- A tool gains an optional input in forge/manifest.yml
- local-forge keeps advertising the old schema (additionalProperties: false), so a skill sending the new key is refused locally but accepted in Forge
- The e2e test stays green because it never reads the manifest

## Expected impact
Either build TOOLS from forge/manifest.yml action inputs at start-up, or add a test that parses the manifest and deep-compares properties/required with TOOLS and the names with TOOL_NAMES; fix the header count.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the local server cannot drift from the deployed contract unnoticed
Before: 3 hand copies (manifest, TOOLS, test list) + TOOL_NAMES; header says seven
After: 1 source; drift fails a test
Method: simulation - walked three cases: an added optional input, a renamed tool, a changed description; each passes today's test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/local-forge.mjs:18 `//     --stdio    an MCP server on stdin/stdout (JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-delimited; framing as the mock): the seven`; tools/local-forge.mjs:53 `// tools/list: scalar input schemas (rovo:mcp allows no arrays), descriptions and properties from forge/manifest.yml.`; skill/scripts/tests/local-forge-e2e.test.mjs:143 `assert.deepEqual(tools.map((t) => t.name), ['dowser_sources_tickets', ...` (literal list); docs/contracts/forge-mcp-2.md:4 `implements these twelve tools`
impact_why: The local loop is the developer's stand-in for Forge; a silent schema drift makes it lie about the contract.

title: Extract the headless-scan harness shared by dogfood and lens-eval
body:
## Summary
tools/dogfood.mjs and tools/lens-eval.mjs carry near-identical copies of cli(), removeWork(), git(), ALLOWED_TOOLS, the unattended prompt and the claude spawn/result block.

## Description
cli(): tools/dogfood.mjs:224-228 vs tools/lens-eval.mjs:219-223 (identical body). removeWork(): tools/dogfood.mjs:231-237 vs tools/lens-eval.mjs:226-232 (identical). ALLOWED_TOOLS: tools/dogfood.mjs:146 vs tools/lens-eval.mjs:47. The claude invocation and failure handling: tools/dogfood.mjs:290-311 vs tools/lens-eval.mjs:258-300. The prompt bullet list: tools/dogfood.mjs:213-221 vs tools/lens-eval.mjs:204-212 (pre-triage and section 9 lines verbatim). forge-live-e2e.mjs:39-43 holds a third cli(). A fix in one (e.g. the Windows .cmd spawn, or a new allowed tool) must be made twice.

## Flow
- The skill gains a tool the scan needs (e.g. a new MCP prefix)
- lens-eval gets the new ALLOWED_TOOLS entry; dogfood does not
- Dogfood scans silently lose a step and the campaign reports look worse for a harness reason

## Expected impact
One tools/lib/headless.mjs (cli, removeWork, git, ALLOWED_TOOLS, runClaude, unattendedPrompt) imported by both tools removes about 60 duplicated lines and one class of drift.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one harness, one place to fix
Before: 2-3 copies of each helper
After: 1 module; both tools import it
Method: simulation - diffed the helper bodies by reading; walked an ALLOWED_TOOLS change and a spawn fix through both tools
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/dogfood.mjs:146 and tools/lens-eval.mjs:47 both `const ALLOWED_TOOLS = ['Bash', 'Read', 'Grep', 'Glob', 'Write', 'Edit', 'Skill', 'mcp__dowser__*'];`; tools/dogfood.mjs:225 and tools/lens-eval.mjs:220 both `const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [CLI, ...args, '--repo', w.repo], { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, DOWSER_HOME: w.home } });`
impact_why: Two eval harnesses that must behave alike drift apart one fix at a time.

title: quality-snapshot reads test counts from spec output: TAP on Node 22 writes null
body:
## Summary
tools/quality-snapshot.mjs parses `ℹ tests N` from `npm test` stdout and ignores the exit status; under a reporter other than spec the row records tests: null and tests_fail: null.

## Description
tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:242-244 runs `npm test` piped and matches `ℹ ${k} (\d+)`. The spec reporter prints `ℹ tests 225` (measured on Node 24). On Node 22 (the engines floor, package.json engines `>=22.13.0`) node --test chose TAP when stdout is not a TTY (spec became the non-TTY default in Node 23), whose summary is `# tests 225`, so `num()` returns NaN and JSON.stringify writes null - a value AGENTS.md "Absent values" forbids - and the --append delta at tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:270 compares against null. A crashed suite also reads as NaN rather than fail, because t.status is never consulted.

## Flow
- A campaign on Node 22 runs quality-snapshot --append
- The row stores "tests": null, "tests_fail": null
- The delta line reads tests 225 -> null, and a failing gate is not recorded as fail

## Expected impact
Make the row reporter-independent: run `node --test --test-reporter=spec ...` directly (or parse both `ℹ`/`#` forms) and record tests_status from t.status; omit the keys when unparsed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the snapshot's gate fields are measured on every supported Node
Before: regex matches only spec output; exit status unused
After: counts parsed on Node 22 and 24; a failing run records fail
Method: simulation - no Node 22 on this machine; probed spec output on Node 24 (`ℹ tests 1`) and walked TAP (`# tests 1`) against the regex
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:242 `const t = spawnSync('npm test', { cwd: ROOT, encoding: 'utf8', shell: true });`; :243 `const num = (k) => Number((t.stdout.match(new RegExp(`ℹ ${k} (\\d+)`)) ?? [])[1] ?? NaN);`; package.json `"node": ">=22.13.0"`; Node 24 probe piped stdout -> `ℹ tests 1`
impact_why: Campaign trend rows silently lose test counts on the supported Node floor; a red suite is not recorded as red.

title: Eval tools spawn CLAUDE_BIN without a shell: an npm-installed claude.cmd fails
body:
## Summary
dogfood, lens-eval and forge-live-e2e call spawnSync/execFileSync(CLAUDE) directly; on Windows a .cmd launcher cannot run that way, though lens-eval's own npm shim already handles the case.

## Description
tools/dogfood.mjs:303 and tools/lens-eval.mjs:292 `spawnSync(CLAUDE, args, ...)`; tools/forge-live-e2e.mjs:56 `execFileSync(process.env.CLAUDE_BIN ?? 'claude', ...)`. Node refuses .cmd/.bat without shell:true (ENOENT for a bare name, EINVAL for an explicit .cmd since the 2024 CVE fix). The same file knows this: tools/lens-eval.mjs:192-194 quotes and runs a .cmd under a shell for npm. It works on this machine only because claude resolves to C:\Users\kazda\.local\bin\claude.exe (native install); an `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` install is claude.cmd.

## Flow
- A Windows contributor with the npm-installed CLI runs `node tools/lens-eval.mjs --lens doc-drift`
- spawnSync returns error ENOENT; status null
- The tool reports "the scan failed (exit null, spawnSync claude ENOENT)" after building the whole workspace

## Expected impact
Resolve the binary once (where/which, prefer .exe, else run the .cmd with shell and quoted args, as the npm shim does) in the shared harness; the eval tools then run for every Windows install.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - eval tools start on every supported claude install
Before: probe: spawnSync('npm', ['-v']) on this Windows box -> status null, ENOENT (npm is a .cmd)
After: the .cmd path is run through the shell, as tools/lens-eval.mjs:194 already does for npm
Method: simulation - probed the same spawn pattern with npm (a .cmd); claude here is an .exe so the exact failure could not be reproduced without installing
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/lens-eval.mjs:292 `const r = spawnSync(CLAUDE, args, { cwd: w.repo, env, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 45 * 60000, maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });`; tools/lens-eval.mjs:192 `'// A .cmd needs a shell on Windows; quote the command and every argument for it.',`; probe `spawnSync('npm',['-v'])` -> `null ENOENT`; `where claude` -> C:\Users\kazda\.local\bin\claude.exe
impact_why: Windows contributors on the npm-installed CLI cannot run any eval or dogfood tool.

title: quality-snapshot --append joins an absolute path under the repo root
body:
## Summary
`--append` is resolved with join(ROOT, appendTo), so an absolute path is glued under the repo instead of honoured.

## Description
tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:255 `const file = join(ROOT, appendTo);`. On POSIX, `--append /tmp/q.jsonl` becomes `<repo>/tmp/q.jsonl` - an untracked file written inside the repository; on Windows `C:\x\q.jsonl` becomes `<repo>\C:\x\q.jsonl`, which fails. The sibling tools resolve their paths (tools/dogfood.mjs:184 `resolve(...)`, tools/sample-capture.mjs:55 `resolve(o.out)`).

## Flow
- A campaign passes --append $CAMPAIGN/quality.jsonl (absolute)
- POSIX: the row lands in <repo>/<campaign path>/quality.jsonl, an untracked file in the repo; the campaign file never grows
- Windows: appendFileSync throws ENOENT

## Expected impact
Use resolve(appendTo) (relative paths still resolve from cwd) so the campaign file is the one written.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the row goes where the flag says
Before: path.posix.join('/repo','/tmp/q.jsonl') -> /repo/tmp/q.jsonl
After: resolve('/tmp/q.jsonl') -> /tmp/q.jsonl
Method: simulation - evaluated path.join on both platforms with node -e; three cases walked (relative, POSIX absolute, Windows absolute)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:255 `const file = join(ROOT, appendTo);`; node -e path.posix.join('/repo','/tmp/q.jsonl') -> `/repo/tmp/q.jsonl`
impact_why: Absolute --append writes inside the repo (POSIX) or crashes (Windows).
